shifts.summary: The first shift was overall moderate in difficulty. Candidates reported attempting between 72 and 80 questions successfully. Reasoning was generally easy with 17–24 good attempts, while General Awareness showed a mixed difficulty and 15–17 good attempts. Quantitative section difficulty varied, with 14–22 good attempts. English difficulty ranged from easy to moderate with 17 good attempts.

intro: The analysis below summarizes the shift‑wise feedback for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 12 October 2026. Unofficial figures suggest that Shift 1 saw roughly 72–80 good attempts and Shift 2 about 75–99, while Shift 3 did not provide reliable attempt counts. Most candidates described the overall difficulty as moderate, with variations across sections. SSC normalises scores across shifts, so direct comparison of raw attempt numbers is not indicative of final marks. Shift 3 has only a limited review available and further corroboration is required.

faqs.q: What overall difficulty level was reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: Across all three shifts on 12 October 2026, candidates most commonly described the paper as moderate in difficulty, though some reports for Shift 3 indicated a slightly harder experience.

faqs.q: How many good attempts were reported for Shift 1 and Shift 2 on 12 October 2026, and are those numbers official?
faqs.a: For Shift 1, candidates mentioned roughly 72–80 good attempts, and for Shift 2 about 75–99 good attempts. These figures are unofficial and should be treated as indicative rather than definitive.

faqs.q: Why is there only a partial analysis for Shift 3 of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 3 has a limited review because the reported data were incomplete and the good‑attempt numbers were not reliably provided. Additional evidence is needed before a full analysis can be published.

faqs.q: Does SSC normalise scores across different shifts for the Tier 1 exam on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes, SSC applies a normalisation process to align scores from the various shifts, ensuring that candidates are evaluated on a comparable basis regardless of the shift they attended.

faqs.q: Are there any pending analyses for any shift of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 12 October 2026?
faqs.a: No usable analysis has been published yet for any pending shift because all three shifts have either reported results or a partial review; no shift remains entirely pending.
